notes: Gzip-9 bytes of each Web-facing entry as scripts/bundle-size.mjs bundles it. baselineGzip is the P1-S19 measurement at 0.25.0, with the Effect core in place; main before the conversion (4f536a8) was 235,346 B at the root and 263,949 B for the Worker example.

Caps: every entry gets baseline + 60,000 B. The conversion-era allowances are retired: the root's flat 386,000 B cap covered a rewrite that is finished, and the +160 KB held for HttpApi in ./ui, ./activity and the Worker example was never spent, because P1-S18 measured HttpApi and did not use it.
A cap moves only in a change that says why. Raising one to make a check pass is the failure this file exists to catch.
./auth/access-tokens starts at 4,222 B gzip in #619. Its legacy record verifier and operator lifecycle use no runtime dependency; the cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./worker starts at 35500 B gzip (#704): bounded admission plus request-owned loader/RPC handle disposal around the optional upstream DynamicWorkerExecutor. The peer stays external; the cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./d1 starts at 2,542 B gzip (#705): the shared SQL key-value and activity store (src/storage/sql.ts) behind a structural D1 driver, with no Effect, no MCP SDK, and no dependency. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy. ./sqlite is its Node-only twin over node:sqlite and is reported, not capped.

examples/worker is remeasured at 395,375 B gzip (#705 item 4): the example now compiles its optional modules — activity history — as type-checked code switched on by its environment, over the D1 store from @zackbart/connecta/d1, where before they were comments outside the bundle. On main (97f25a9, after #722) the same example measured 360,549 B on the same machine. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

Phase 4 item 1 (#708) replaces Preact with production React, Radix, TanStack Router/Query/Table and cmdk, plus Tailwind v4 and locally hosted Inter. Assets measure 650.4 KB minified/raw and 218,702 B gzip summed per HTTP payload, including the font and license notices. The ./ui server entry embeds this portable asset manifest for Node and Workers (272,943 B gzip); the Worker example remeasures at 586,559 B. Each gzip cap retains baseline + 60,000 B; assets also cap raw bytes at 700,000 B. This is a deliberate stack migration: small uncached HTML responses now refer to reusable immutable assets rather than repeating inline browser code. React and all browser libraries remain build dependencies, outside the root import graph.

Phase 2 item 2 (#706, PR #739) remeasures the typed guest API: root 339,882 B gzip, ./worker 74,666 B, and examples/worker 649,045 B. Acorn is the Worker import router's parser and also checks that a guest program is one expression before splicing; syntax-aware parsing prevents imports from reaching private runner modules. The named ESM parse import is already used, and Acorn exports no smaller parse-only entry. Esbuild attribution confirms Acorn is absent from the root graph; root growth over main is the typed guest outcomes, diagnostics, and runtime hardening. These entries use the measured baseline + 60,000 B policy.
./providers/basecamp starts at 131,228 B gzip, measured where it was introduced: a remoteMcp() wrapper like ./providers/revenuecat, so the same shape and the same baseline + 60,000 B policy.
./providers/breeze starts at 20,637 B gzip: a hand-written api() surface with no hosted-MCP interface, so it carries no MCP SDK. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/ccb starts at 120,479 B gzip: the hand-written surface plus api()'s static OAuth grant over the SDK's auth client, with no remoteMcp() transport. The cap uses the baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/docs starts at 27,149 B gzip (#681): the same class as ./providers/gmail — a hand-written api() surface over the shared Workspace delegation layer, with no OAuth client and no MCP SDK. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/drive starts at 28,955 B gzip (#680): the same class as ./providers/gmail — a hand-written api() surface over the shared Workspace delegation layer, with two confined transports (API and upload host) and no MCP SDK. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/forms starts at 26,161 B gzip (#684): the same class as ./providers/gmail — a hand-written api() surface over the shared Workspace delegation layer, with no OAuth client and no MCP SDK. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/github initial measured baseline includes the hosted MCP SDK plus portable GitHub App signing, exact routing and REST complements; cap retains the existing 60,000-byte provider headroom policy.

./providers/gmail starts at 27,085 B gzip (#678): a hand-written api() surface over the guarded transport plus the shared Google Workspace delegation layer — Web Crypto RS256 signing, an in-memory token cache, result-size budgeting, bound cursors, and request-outcome tracking, with no OAuth client and no MCP SDK. The other Workspace products share that layer and should land in the same class. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/infisical starts at 27,673 B gzip (#677): guarded transport, Universal Auth request-local flights and eight named tools, with no MCP client or Effect runtime. The cap uses the measured baseline plus the existing 60,000 B headroom policy.

./providers/notion remeasures at 211,735 B gzip (#801), against a 145,300 B baseline: auth now selects the implementation, so the entry carries the hosted MCP client and Connecta's REST connector (api(), the schema validator, guarded transport, the shared REST module) plus the pinned Notion operation index (64 operations; request details to depth 4, so block payload keys validate, with 160-character top-level descriptions; 14,240 B gzip as source). The index is already small, and removing eight one-operation named tools offset part of the shared module, so shrinking details further could not bring the entry under the old cap. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/overflow starts at 20,410 B gzip: a hand-written api() surface over the guarded transport with no hosted-MCP interface, so it pulls in neither remoteMcp nor the Effect core the other providers carry. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/planning-center starts at 26,970 B gzip. It is api() over the guarded transport with no hosted-MCP surface, so neither the MCP client nor the Effect core is in its graph; the cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/sheets starts at 26,026 B gzip (#682): the same class as ./providers/gmail — a hand-written api() surface over the shared Workspace delegation layer, with no OAuth client and no MCP SDK. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.

./providers/slides starts at 29,685 B gzip (#683): a hand-written api() surface on the shared Workspace delegation layer, like ./providers/gmail, and larger than it for what keeps every read deliverable and recoverable — reading-order projection, element- and character-level continuation, raw JSON chunking, and revision-bound cursors. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy. Comments (#696) — a thread read that pages text across results with a raw mode, six comment writes, partial-save reporting, and ids-first raw replies — move the measured size to 35,074 B; the cap stays at 89,685 B, set from the 29,685 B first measurement.

./providers/stripe remeasures at 232,089 B gzip (#801), from 170,771 B on main: auth now selects the implementation, so the entry carries the hosted MCP client and Connecta's REST connector (api(), the schema validator, guarded transport, the shared REST module) plus the pinned Stripe operation index (638 operations; request details to depth 2, without descriptions or enums over 50 values; 37,918 B gzip as source). Details were shrunk before the cap moved: the first full index measured 81 KB gzip. The cap uses the existing baseline + 60,000 B policy.
